blockers.detail: The claim requires physical free-space optical (FSO) terminal hardware or a validated atmospheric-optical propagation model to evaluate link availability under severe cloud cover. No such equipment or model is available.
blockers.required_input: Optical terminal hardware (or access to a validated FSO channel simulator) capable of measuring link availability under controlled or observed cloud-cover conditions.

blockers.detail: The registered runners (emulated-netem-v1, real-world-iperf-v1) operate at the IP/transport layer and cannot model or measure optical-atmospheric phenomena such as beam attenuation by cloud particles.
blockers.required_input: A runner or validated simulation tool that models free-space optical link behavior under varying atmospheric conditions (cloud optical depth, visibility, water content).

blockers.detail: No atmospheric or optical measurement data (e.g., cloud optical depth, link margin, received optical power, weather observations) is supplied to evaluate the claim.
blockers.required_input: Empirical or simulated data on optical-link availability metrics (received power, BER, link margin) correlated with cloud-cover severity measurements.

input.reason: The claim concerns physical optical terminals remaining available during severe local cloud cover. This is an atmospheric/optical-physics phenomenon: cloud particles attenuate or block free-space optical (FSO) links. Assessing this claim requires (1) actual optical terminal hardware or a validated atmospheric-optical channel model, and (2) real or rigorously modeled cloud-cover conditions (e.g., optical depth, water content, visibility). The two registered runners (emulated-netem-v1, real-world-iperf-v1) are IP-layer networking tools that measure packet delay/loss/throughput; they cannot establish anything about optical-link availability under cloud cover. A flow_completion_time_ms metric over an emulated network path does not replicate or validate the physical optical propagation phenomenon. No registered check applies, and no equipment or validated domain model is available to test this claim.
